Spool depth that raises one backlog alert.

Empty by default since BH-1510.2: the floor runner is the runner on model_routes role 'housekeeping.floor' rung 0, read through bin/lib/lane-model.sh:lane_housekeeping_floor. Set this only to override that row.

Empty by default since BH-1510.2: the model is a database row, model_routes role 'housekeeping.floor' rung 0, read through bin/lib/lane-model.sh:lane_housekeeping_floor. Set this only to override that row on this box/lane; no reviewed min/max, nothing is clamped.

Evidence byte cap for ONE run of this lane. Unset follows the lane's row in catalog/lane-caps.conf; too small and a family is re-spooled every tick and never triaged (it pages once a day and bills nothing).
Retry a cliff-routed family on the floor tier. 0 turns the retry off.
Cliff refusals for one family before it stops being re-spooled. Nothing is called and nothing is billed on a refusal.

Hours before STEP 0 retires a merge-conductor per-PR BUDGET NOTE (bin/triage-spool-retire.sh rule 1). Parks (BLOCKED_HUMAN, RED_TWICE) and the stuck detector are excluded and live out TRIAGE_SPOOL_MAX_AGE_H.
Per-session context ceiling for THIS lane only, exported to agent-call.sh as CONTEXT_KILL_TOKENS. Unset/0 means catalog/context-budgets.json decides, so the manifest stays the single source.

0 makes this lane call no model at all. bin/lib/llm-gate.sh refuses BEFORE the vendor call and writes a zero-cost row_source=refused row, so the stop is visible in the ledger rather than being a lane that went quiet.

Comma/space list of the ONLY ladder rungs this lane may reach. Empty is every rung, i.e. today's ladder unchanged. A rung outside the list is refused before the call, so a cliff or a failure on the standing lane cannot descend into one that costs ~100x (#1141, the $793 descent).

Dollars this lane may spend in the current UTC day, summed from D1 cost_rows through GET /api/metrics/llm-spend — never from the box's own logs/cost.csv. A second, project-scoped ceiling is the lane.<id>.<project>.llm_usd_cap_day row, which is read only when somebody wrote it.

Dollars this lane may spend in one UTC day, resolved by bin/lib/lane-caps.sh over catalog/lane-caps.conf (now: 5). 0 STOPS the lane; `off` runs it uncapped; nothing is dropped when it trips — the queue waits and it pages once a day. This is the cap BH-1039 added after alert-triage burned $793 in 12 hours inside its session cap.

Hold [orchestrator/merge-conductor] alert lines (re-spooled, not sessioned) while the conductor publishes kill-switch, observe or no mode at all (unknown). 0 makes this lane ignore the conductor's mode.

Sessions concluding `handled=0 escalated=0` this lane may buy in one UTC day, resolved by bin/lib/lane-caps.sh over the `noise` rows of catalog/lane-caps.conf (now: 10). At the budget the lane stops buying sessions until 00:00Z and pages once; a session that handles or escalates anything resets the count. 0 STOPS the lane; `off` runs it unbounded; nothing is dropped — the queue waits. BH-1168, after 150 of 192 sessions on 2026-09-20 concluded handled=0 escalated=0 at ~$4 each.
